readme: What has been looked at in the owner's Kenney packs, and what each region is.
This is metadata, not art: it names regions of packs that live on the owner's
machine and never enter this repository. Committing it is what makes looking at
a pack a one-time cost -- the next curation session reads this instead of
Classification is ON DEMAND. Only regions relevant to giri's thirteen asset
slots (UI.md section 9) are classified; everything else is listed under
'unclassified' with its extent, so a later session knows what was skipped
rather than guessing it was empty. Labelling a whole pack would be hours spent
It lives with giri until a second game wants it (second-consumer rule).
Regenerate contact sheets with art/contact_sheet.py; sheets are never
committed -- a whole pack rearranged into sheets is still the whole pack.
Every pack is CC0 1.0 (each pack's own License.txt, quoted in assets/CREDITS.md).
Kenney *requests* that whole packs not be redistributed; that is not a licence
term, and the curation model honours it by construction.

micro-roguelike.name: Micro Roguelike (1.3)
micro-roguelike.note: Clean transparent-background silhouettes at 8x8 -- giri's stat icons are drawn at exactly this size.

tiny-dungeon.name: Tiny Dungeon (1.0)
tiny-dungeon.note: Head-and-shoulders character busts at 16x16, plus full-bleed dungeon tiles.

roguelike-characters.name: Roguelike Characters pack (2.0)
roguelike-characters.note: Mostly a modular paper doll -- torsos, helmets, weapons as separate cells. Only the assembled busts listed below are usable as a portrait without compositing.

1-bit-pack.name: 1-Bit Pack (1.2)
1-bit-pack.note: Two-tone. Swept for an eye glyph (see 'gaps'); nothing else classified -- the palette does not sit with the coloured packs.

cartography-pack.name: Cartography Pack (1.0)
cartography-pack.note: Descriptive filenames (tower, graveyard, mine, chest) that read like giri's quest types -- but 64x64 into a 72-unit slot is a fractional scale, which UI.md section 1.4 forbids. Excluded from candidates for that reason alone; recorded here so the next session does not re-derive it.

generic-items.name: Generic Items #1
generic-items.note: Roughly 75x86 and painterly, not pixel art. Not classified: nothing at giri's sizes.

platformer-characters-1.name: Platformer Characters 1 (1.0)
platformer-characters-1.note: Large multi-frame animation sheets. Not classified: nothing at giri's sizes.

gaps.finding: No eye glyph exists in any of the seven packs.
gaps.looked_at: All 160 Micro Roguelike tiles, all 132 Tiny Dungeon tiles, all 83 Cartography filenames, and the 1-Bit Pack's symbol band (cells 661-1077, which holds its UI glyphs). The 1-Bit cells that read as eyes at thumbnail size (705-717) are targeting reticles.
gaps.consequence: UI.md section 2 fixes 'eye icon = infamy' as a stable signifier; changing it is a UI.md edit and the owner's call, not an import detail. The slot therefore keeps its generated icon unless the owner decides otherwise -- import_pack.py's partial-library path is exactly this case.

_note: What the owner picked, 2026-08-23, from the shortlists in target/giri-art/.
Role -> manifest entry id. null means the role keeps its generated art.
This is the curation record: art/extract.py reads it to stage role-named PNGs,
and import_pack.py copies those into assets/. Re-running both reproduces the
committed library from the owner's packs exactly.
Portrait assignment to characters is by temperament, not by any described
appearance -- DESIGN gives the four no faces, only social roles. Swapping two
portraits is a one-line edit here plus a re-run.
